lines: A Hawaiian bay disappeared in less than a week.
Then, on May 3rd, the ground under a neighborhood split open. Twenty-four fissures.
From orbit, Landsat's infrared picked up the heat.
One vent sent lava all the way to the ocean.
It reached Kapoho Bay on June 3rd. By June 7th, the bay was gone.
Nearly fourteen square miles of lava. Over eighteen hundred structures destroyed.
Meanwhile, as magma drained away, the summit collapsed.
The caldera floor dropped more than sixteen hundred feet.
Hawaii gained eight hundred seventy-five acres of new land.
Who owns it? Not the neighbors. Under a 1977 court ruling, it belongs to the State.
